description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/lock.t is five rows and PCL produces NONE of them: each of
    is \lock $foo, \$foo
    is  lock @foo, \@foo
    is  lock %foo, \%foo
    is  lock &foo, \&foo
    is  lock &eulavl, \&eulavl     # sub eulavl : lvalue { $x }
reaches the runtime with the wrong arity ("invalid number of arguments: N") and
aborts its top-level form -- the runner records `aborted-forms:5:`.

In a perl built without threads, `lock` is a NO-OP whose value is a REFERENCE
to its argument, and that is exactly what the file tests.  So the whole file is
one small runtime function plus the `(\[$@%&*];)` prototype shape that lets
`lock @foo` take the ARRAY rather than its elements.

The last row also needs NS:Lvalue subroutines [DEFERRED] (#930), so four of the
five are reachable.
subject: `lock` is not implemented: in a non-threaded perl it is a no-op that RETURNS A REF to its argument; PCL aborts the form (op/lock.t, all 5 rows + 5 shortfall)
